data.long_meaning: Madhan is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'madh' which means 'nectar' or 'sweet'. The name Madhan carries the meaning “God, Lord” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. data.spiritual_symbolism: Madhan is a Sanskrit name, derived from the word 'Madh' meaning 'nectar'. The name is a reminder to always stay in the state of divine intoxication, transcending worldly desires.

historical_references.reference: According to Hindu mythology, Lord Krishna is also known as Madhana Mohana or Madhava, which means 'he who intoxicates and attracts'. This name is derived from the incident where Lord Krishna stole the butter from the house of his foster mother Yasoda. He was intoxicated by the taste of the butter and thus, the name Madhana Mohana or Madhava was given to him. This incident is believed to have occurred during Lord Krishna's childhood.

Another reference to the name Madhan is found in the Harivansh Purana. In this epic, King Madhava is described as the ruler of the Vrishni kingdom. He is also known as Madhava because of his association with Lord Krishna. Madhava is said to have ruled during the late Mahabharata period, around 3138-3102 BC.

It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
